text: Wedge-tailed Eagles. Wedge-tailed eagles are the largest birds of prey in Australia, with wings that can stretch more than two metres from tip to tip. They can soar higher than almost any other Australian bird, sometimes more than a kilometre above the ground. Pairs often stay together for many years and return to the same nesting area each spring. frame: Gus is writing a report called 'The Human Nose'. The Fittlet swallowed one of his sub-headings.
text: ___ Snot might be revolting, but your body would be in serious trouble without it. Its first job is to trap things. Every time you breathe in, the sticky snot lining your nose catches dust, pollen and germs before they can reach your lungs. Its second job is to keep the inside of your nose moist, because a dry nose cracks and bleeds easily. Some snot even traps specks of smoke and tiny bugs, holding them until they can be swept away. Snot also warms and dampens the air on its way in, so that cold, dry air doesn't irritate your lungs. It even contains special chemicals that attack some germs, which means it works a little like a security guard at the door. Without snot, every breath would carry dirt and germs straight into your chest. Tiny hairs called cilia sweep the dirty snot towards the back of your throat, where you swallow it without noticing, dust and all. When you catch a cold, your nose makes extra snot to flush the germs out, which is why it runs. Your nose makes fresh snot all day long, so this protection never runs out. So the next time you need a tissue, remember that your snot is busy keeping you healthy.
